co_second_pew.blurb: Second Pew is a granite face in the Pulpit Rock Massif above Cow Creek Canyon, in the Estes Park valley. It is a broad, wide formation set a couple of rock layers behind Pulpit Rock itself, with a smooth upper left and a more featured right side that can give long outings. The ten routes here are all traditional, running from easy fifth class through the 5.8 range up to a couple of 5.10s and one 5.11. Expect a quiet, adventurous place where you place your own gear, with a few bolts mixed in and ice sometimes lingering in the cave early in the season.

co_strategery_wall.blurb: Strategery Wall is a bolted limestone wall in Lime Creek canyon, reached by forest roads from the Eagle and Red Cliff side of the Rockies, at roughly 9,200 feet. All ten lines are sport routes, spanning the 5.10s through the low 5.12s, with a handful of well-rated lines and nothing harder than 12c. The wall faces east and has no trees to shade it, so expect sun in the morning. The walk in follows a creek trail and then a steep climbers' path uphill. Some lines are marked as projects or carry loose rock, so inspect before you commit.

co_seven_bridges.blurb: Seven Bridges is a small bouldering zone along the Seven Bridges Trail in North Cheyenne Canyon on the west side of Colorado Springs, at about 6,500 feet. Its centrepiece is a huge bolted boulder that the trail passes beneath, with other problems just before and after it. Ten problems are recorded, a mix that stretches from easy VB-to-V0 warm-ups through the middle grades to several hard lines in the V6 to V8 range. The granite canyon is shaded and creekside, so it is a pleasant spot for a short session, though the problems are few and spread along the hike.

co_slabs_the.blurb: The Slabs is the western end of the Ophir Wall, a high-elevation cliff in the old mining town of Ophir in the San Juan Mountains south of Telluride. The ten routes here lean toward traditional lines, with a few bolted ones, and they are mostly lower-angle friction climbing with a few steeper crack and face pitches mixed in. Grades run from easy fifth class through the 5.7 and 5.8 range to a handful of 5.10s and one 5.11. It suits climbers who like old-school, thoughtful movement and are comfortable placing their own protection.

co_sidewinder_canyon.blurb: Sidewinder Canyon is a quiet side canyon in the San Luis Valley, one of four canyons that make up the Penitente climbing area near La Garita, at about 8,000 feet. All ten routes are bolted sport climbs on volcanic rock, with most in the 5.11 range, several at 5.12 and one at 5.13. The best lines sit on the north-side wall. There is no real trail inside the canyon, so you follow the wash until you reach the climbing. It is remote and uncrowded, a good pick for strong sport climbers; watch for rattlesnakes in warm weather.
